slides.stem: If $4x^2 + kx + 49$ is a perfect square trinomial, where $k$ is a constant, what are all possible values of $k$?

slides.body: A perfect square here means $(2x \pm 7)^2$, and the middle term is $\pm 2(2x)(7) = \pm 28x$. Both versions expand to the same first and last terms, so $k$ can be $28$ or $-28$. The question says "all possible values" for a reason.

slides.title: Squares hide a second sign
slides.body:
$(2x + 7)^2$ and $(2x - 7)^2$ have identical ends and opposite middles. Whenever a square is involved, ask whether the negative case works too.

"All possible values" in the stem is the SAT telling you the answer isn't single.
